message.reasoning_content:
The user asks about Kubernetes v1.34 version-skew policy for kubelet/kubectl vs kube-apiserver. Need to search official docs.

Known policy: kubelet may be older by up to 3 minor versions than kube-apiserver; kubectl supported within one minor version of kube-apiserver (+/-1). But in v1.34, changes: kubelet skew policy changed? Let me recall: Kubernetes 1.28 changed kubelet skew from +2/-2 to older versions. Actually official policy: kube-apiserver must be within one minor of kubelet, and kubelet may be older by up to 3. For kubectl: within one minor version of kube-apiserver. Also 1.34 changed "kubelet may be newer"? There was a KEP about allowing kubelet newer. Let me verify via docs.

Actually the version skew policy doc: "kubelet may be up to three minor versions older than kube-apiserver" and "A kubelet may not be newer than the kube-apiserver version"? Hmm, there's a change in 1.34: kubelet skew policy changed to allow kubelet newer? Let me check: KEP-5011? Not sure. The policy doc says kubectl: "kubectl is supported within one minor version (older or newer) of kube-apiserver." Example: if kube-apiserver is at 1.34, kubectl 1.33, 1.34, and 1.35 are supported.

HA at 1.33 and 1.34: intersection for kubectl: must be within one minor of every apiserver. For 1.33: 1.32-1.34; for 1.34: 1.33-1.35. Intersection: 1.33, 1.34. So kubectl 1.35 not supported. Once all servers 1.34: kubectl 1.33, 1.34, 1.35 supported.

Also v1.34 policy may include note: kubelet may be newer? Confirm with fetching docs. Also policy for other components e.g. kube-proxy. Fetch https://kubernetes.io/docs/setup/release/version-skew-policy/ → now at /releases/version-skew-policy/. Let's search and fetch.
